title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 44 (Effect of release of one joint promisor)

content.overview: Section 44 provides that where two or more persons have made a joint promise, a release of one of such joint promisors by the promisee does not discharge the other joint promisor or joint promisors; neither does it free the joint promisor so released from responsibility to the other joint promisor or joint promisors.
content.glance: Release of one joint promisor does not discharge the others; released promisor remains responsible to the other joint promisors.
content.study: A release by the promisee of one joint promisor does not discharge the other joint promisor(s). The released promisor also remains responsible to the other joint promisor(s) (e.g. for contribution). Current-law framing: identify release of one joint promisor; apply non-discharge of the others; apply continuing responsibility of the released promisor inter se.

sections.heading: Others not discharged
sections.body: Release of one joint promisor by the promisee does not discharge the other joint promisor or joint promisors.

sections.heading: Released promisor still responsible inter se
sections.body: Does not free the released joint promisor from responsibility to the other joint promisor or joint promisors.

provisions.title: Effect of release of one joint promisor

examples.title: Release of one of three
examples.body: A, B and C jointly promise to pay D. D releases A. B and C remain liable to D; A remains responsible to B and C inter se under s. 44.

hypotheticals.question: Does releasing one joint promisor free everyone?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 44: the others remain liable to the promisee, and the released promisor remains responsible to the other joint promisors.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-44
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Release of one joint promisor discharges all under common-law joint obligation rules.
misconceptions.correction: Section 44 expressly preserves the liability of the other joint promisors and inter se responsibility of the released promisor.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 44 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify release of one joint promisor. II. Apply non-discharge of others. III. Apply continuing inter se responsibility. IV. Conclude.

examTips: State both limbs: others not discharged; released still responsible inter se.
revisionPoints: Released promisor still responsible inter se
